newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Dossetti, political figure, dies.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dossetti, political figure, dies.

text.p: Giuseppe Dossetti, a Roman Catholic priest active Italy's post-war politics and credited with being one of the founders of the Christian Democratic party, died on Sunday at age 83.
Doctors said Dossetti died of cardiac arrest in hospital near Bologna.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said Dossetti was "one of the principal drafters of our Constitution and our democratic life".

Dossetti became involved in politics after taking part in the partisan movement during World War Two. He rose quickly through party ranks to become vice-secretary of the Christian Democrat (DC) party, which dominated Italian politics until its downfall in corruption probes in the early 1990s.

He left the party and gave up his seat in parliament in 1953 to set up a centre for religious studies in Bologna. He later returned to politics, becoming involved in local Bologna affairs as well as continuing his Church work.
